correctness.rationale: Exactly three floor blocks of sizes summing to at most five have only the four partitions (1,1,1), (2,1,1), (2,2,1), (3,1,1). The block-suffix outcome probabilities obey the matrix displayed in RESULT.md. Thirteen listed maximal minors have determinant +1 or -1, hence each matrix has independent columns. At surplus 0 and n there is one outcome. The six-party two-lottery example has exactly the required six marginal round-up probabilities, fixed total surplus three and zero envy. Independent exact rational Gaussian elimination, exact minor determinants and a computer algebra cross-check reproduced the finite certificates.

originality.rationale: The established general envy-free flow LP specifies existence, not the sharp universal distributional uniqueness cutoff. Known two-stratum uniqueness and six-party three-pair transportation families do not state or imply a general three-stratum all-shape at-most-five-party uniqueness theorem without the new complete rank classification. Specific two-by-two-plus-singleton feasibility inequalities are not claimed as new, as they are reducible to six-party three-pair results by complements and padding.
residual_risks: An unindexed prior exact smallest-size distributional uniqueness theorem is possible.
The general published flow program contains an implicit computational route to the same finite property; it should not be represented as independent new algorithmic solvability.
Some older closely related lottery papers were checked only by abstract rather than full text; independent audit remains unperformed.

value.rationale: The exact first possible loss of distributional uniqueness answers a natural mechanism-design identifiability question, not just whether zero-envy allocations exist. With three floor groups and at most five parties, all fair correlations are forced by marginal entitlements; six permits a genuine choice of correlation, exhibited by two rational lotteries. This sharp boundary comprises every small block-size configuration, rather than an arbitrary fixed numerical slice, and distinguishes rigid from non-rigid fairness mechanisms.
